entries.17cb228ba877fbc4: A company that makes automotive interior components such as seats and door trims, and parts such as filters, and supplies them mainly to the [[company:toyota|Toyota Motor]] group.
entries.17eaf060f30530fc: Its principal customer is [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]] and its group companies, which record revenue in all reportable segments; their revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,489,792 million (¥1,422,366 million in the previous fiscal year). By counterparty, sales were ¥478,328 million to TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION (23.5% of total sales), ¥255,384 million to Toyota Motor North America, Inc. (12.5%), and ¥204,578 million to Toyota Auto Body Co., Ltd. (10.0%). Orders are placed mainly on the basis of quarterly and next-month production plans provided by each customer, led by TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION; the company draws up its own production plan in light of its production capacity and manufactures accordingly. Selling prices are set by proposing a desired price that takes market prices and total costs into account, then negotiating individually. The company also purchases automotive parts from TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION and its subsidiaries; in the fiscal year ended March 2026 these purchases were ¥135,294 million.
entries.1c90118b2c8d958f: This is a business in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Brazil and Argentina. Toyota Boshoku America Co., Ltd. (Kentucky, USA) oversees the business, and subsidiaries in Tennessee, Indiana, Illinois and Kentucky in the United States, Ontario in Canada, and the city of Buenos Aires in Argentina, among others, have production facilities for automotive parts. Toyota Boshoku America Co., Ltd.'s revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding internal revenue between consolidated companies) was ¥513,360 million, and it is a company whose share of consolidated revenue exceeds 10%. Revenue from external customers in the North, Central and South America segment was ¥537,656 million (up 11.1% year on year), second only to Japan in scale. The company explains that revenue increased due to growth in production volumes and changes in model mix.

entries.2249299003ce429f: The group consists of TOYOTA BOSHOKU CORPORATION (the filing company), 69 consolidated subsidiaries, 20 equity-method affiliates, and [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]], for which the company is an affiliate, and its main activities are the manufacture and sale of automotive parts and textile products. The 5 regions of Japan, North and South America, China, Asia, and Europe and Africa are the reportable [[term:segment|segments]]; local subsidiaries in each region draw up comprehensive strategies and carry out business, and the 5 regions are managed as 1 management unit. The number of employees is 45,521 (fiscal year ended March 2026). As of March 31, 2026, TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION is the largest shareholder, holding 32.43% of the issued shares (excluding treasury shares).

entries.40306cee97f60006: Profit attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥23,271 million, up 39.2% from ¥16,719 million in the previous fiscal year. Because the consolidated financial statements are prepared under [[term:ifrs|International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)]], the terms revenue and profit differ from net sales and net income under Japanese standards. As efforts supporting profit, the company explains that, building on an integrated development and production system from component parts through to finished products, it continues to improve production processes using the Toyota Production System (TPS) and DX, and to reduce costs through cost planning and VA (a method of lowering costs by changing design or processes without reducing quality or functionality). Because sales to TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION account for 23.5% of revenue, the company cites TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION's automobile sales trends as a factor affecting its operating results.

entries.7b136e4d619d62ef: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥2,037,063 million, up 4.2% from ¥1,954,218 million in the previous fiscal year. The company attributes this to increased production in North, Central and South America and new product launches in Japan, among other factors. Revenue from external customers by regional reportable segment (change from the previous year) was: Japan ¥891,184 million (up 3.2%), North, Central and South America ¥537,656 million (up 11.1%), Asia ¥285,145 million (up 5.9%), China ¥202,377 million (down 8.9%), and Europe and Africa ¥120,698 million (up 4.6%); China alone recorded a decline in revenue. The company cites, as factors with a significant impact on its operating results, changes in the production volumes, sales volumes and vehicle models of its customer automakers. In the medium-term management plan announced in November 2023, the company sets a 2030 financial target of revenue of ¥2.2 trillion.

TOYOTA BOSHOKU CORPORATION (the company) is in charge, and at factories in Aichi and Gifu prefectures and elsewhere it manufactures interior components such as automotive seats, door trims and molded headliners, and unit parts such as filters and motor cores for hybrid systems. Domestic subsidiaries include Toyota Boshoku Tohoku Co., Ltd. (Kitakami, Iwate Prefecture), Toyota Boshoku Kyushu Co., Ltd. (Kanzaki, Saga Prefecture), Toyota Boshoku Seiko Co., Ltd. (Takahama, Aichi Prefecture), Araco Co., Ltd., Toyota Boshoku Hirose Co., Ltd., Koberuku Co., Ltd., and TB Logistics Co., Ltd., which handles transportation. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥891,184 million (up 3.2% year on year), the largest region among the five reportable segments. The company explains that revenue increased due to the introduction of new products, among other factors. The main customer is [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]] and its group companies; of the group's revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026, sales to TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION were ¥478,328 million and sales to Toyota Auto Body Co., Ltd. were ¥204,578 million.
entries.8cfba5e6a9fc1b37: What it makes are automotive parts, and revenue from external customers for items other than automotive parts is minimal. The R&D disclosure of the reporting company lists two business divisions: the Mobility Space (Seats, Interior and Exterior) Business and the Unit Parts Business. The former covers seats, door trims and molded headliners, aims to propose planning for the entire mobility space, and is developing the multifunctional block seat 'TBlocks' and door trims with surface-emitting illumination decoration. The latter covers filters (FPT products) and electric products; in addition to motor cores for hybrid systems, it is advancing development of a general-purpose small fuel cell stack that can be mounted on automated transport equipment and other machines. The company describes its 2030 aspiration as 'a company that creates comfortable mobility spaces as an interior space creator and contributes to solving social issues while expanding its range of products and customers.'
